hints: The program squares everything. Which method keeps only some items?
Call numbers.filter(n => n % 2 === 0) first, then .map(n => n * n) on the result.
This trips up lots of people. Filter first, then map, because mapping first would square the odd numbers too. Here is the complete code.

python.starterCode:
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
result = list(map(lambda n: n * n, numbers))
print(" ".join(map(str, result)))
hints: The program squares everything. Which function keeps only some items?
Wrap numbers in filter(lambda n: n % 2 == 0, numbers) before mapping the squares.
This trips up lots of people. Filter first, then map, because mapping first would square the odd numbers too. Here is the complete code.
python.answerCode:
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
result = list(map(lambda n: n * n, filter(lambda n: n % 2 == 0, numbers)))
print(" ".join(map(str, result)))
